gloss: chimaki, rice dumpling wrapped in bamboo leaf

definitions.gloss: chimaki, rice dumpling wrapped in bamboo leaf
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese confection of glutinous rice or rice flour wrapped in bamboo or reed leaves and steamed. Eaten especially during the Boys' Day festival on May 5th.

examples.japanese: ちまき⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
⟦{端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく}→端午の節句：16518_tangonosekku⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ちまき⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: We eat chimaki on Boys' Day.

examples.japanese: ⟦{笹|ささ}の{葉|は}→笹の葉：18967_sasanoha⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{包|つつ}んだ→包む：01226_tsutsumu⟧ちまき⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{甘|あま}くて→甘い：00617_amai⟧⟦もちもち→もちもち：05260_mochimochi⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Chimaki wrapped in bamboo leaves are sweet and chewy.

notes:
WRITING:
Can be written as {粽|ちまき}, but the hiragana form is standard.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditionally eaten on ⟦{端午|たんご}の{節句|せっく}→端午の節句：16518_tangonosekku⟧ (Boys' Day, May 5th) along with ⟦{柏餅|かしわもち}→柏餅：19485_kashiwamochi⟧. The custom originates from China, where rice dumplings were thrown into the river to honor the poet Qu Yuan. In the Kansai region, ちまき tends to be a sweet confection, while in other regions the contents may vary.

REGIONAL VARIATION:
- Kansai: sweet glutinous rice wrapped in ⟦{笹|ささ}→笹：04407_sasa⟧ (bamboo grass)
- Chinese-style: savory fillings with meat and mushrooms

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ちまき⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧: to make chimaki
- ちまき⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧: to eat chimaki
- ⟦{笹|ささ}→笹：04407_sasa⟧{巻|ま}きちまき: bamboo-leaf-wrapped chimaki
